gloss: to glare; to give a piercing look; to stare sharply

definitions.gloss: to glare; to give a piercing look; to stare sharply
definitions.explanation: To look at someone with a single, sharp, intentional gaze that conveys displeasure, suspicion, or intimidation.

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}にジロリと{見|み}られた。
examples.english: The teacher gave me a sharp look.

examples.japanese: {遅刻|ちこく}して{入|はい}ると、{上司|じょうし}がジロリとこちらを{見|み}た。
examples.english: When I came in late, the boss shot me a glare.

examples.japanese: {電車|でんしゃ}の{中|なか}で{大声|おおごえ}で{話|はな}していたら、{隣|となり}の{乗客|じょうきゃく}にジロリと{見|み}られて{恥|は}ずかしくなった。
examples.english: When I was talking loudly on the train, a nearby passenger glared at me and I felt embarrassed.

notes:
Combines the onomatopoeia ジロリ (a sharp, sudden gaze) with と{見|み}る (to look). ジロリ captures a single, deliberate glance — quick but intense, carrying clear disapproval or warning. Written in katakana to emphasize the mimetic quality.

USAGE:
ジロリ describes a momentary look, unlike ジロジロ (repeated staring). One glare from the corner of the eye is ジロリ; sustained, uncomfortable staring is ジロジロ.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ジロリと{見|み}る: to glare at
- ジロリと{見|み}られる: to be glared at (passive)
- ジロリと{睨|にら}む: to glare menacingly

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ジロジロ{見|み}る: to stare rudely — repeated, sustained, and rude staring
- {睨|にら}む: to glare; to stare down — a more intense, hostile gaze
- チラリと{見|み}る: to glance briefly — a quick look without the negative nuance
- じっと{見|み}る: to gaze fixedly — sustained looking, but not necessarily hostile
